findings.text: blocking: the scheduler binary is resolved as Path(argv[0]).with_name("squeue"), but for a placed worker argv[0] is the host-shim srun. The reviewed run's own worker.json records argv[0] = /home/ITER/mcintos/Code/reckon/reckon/host_shims/srun, and that host_shims directory holds only salloc, sbatch and srun — there is no squeue beside it (squeue resolves on PATH to /usr/bin/squeue, and host_shims sits ahead of /usr/bin). So subprocess.run raises FileNotFoundError, the except (OSError, ...) returns None, and signal_pending_step_client can never reach its identity check or its single TERM: the function degrades to the unreadable-scheduler branch for every shim-launched placed worker and is retried each poll forever. Reproduced: calling signal_pending_step_client(101, run) with argv[0] set to the shim path returns None and writes no senders.jsonl (squeue_next_to_shim_exists=False, os.kill guarded so no signal is sent). The reinstated pending-step stop that this commit exists to deliver is therefore inert in production, so a step-placed run whose srun request never started still holds its slot — the exact condition the commit was written to fix. The four unit tests cannot catch this because they monkeypatch process_signal.subprocess.run wholesale and pass argv[0]="/usr/bin/srun", so the executable path is never resolved against the filesystem; the fix is to resolve the scheduler through the same shutil.which used at reckon/crew/dispatch_launch.py:1104 rather than deriving it from argv[0].

follow-on: assert sent == [(101, signal.SIGTERM)] and assert ended == [101] compare against pid 101, which is the same value the test hands to _reap_worker_on_its_terminal_manifest at the call and writes into worker.json, and the signal_step stub also rechecks it (assert pid == 101 at line 289); the receipt assertion at line 344 likewise rechecks entry["target_pid"] against that same 101. All three move with the input, so none independently protects the signal target — a defect that signalled a wrong-but-in-range pid would be handed the wrong value on both sides. The independent guards are the assert sent == [] branches in the named-step and record-present cases, which do redden under the reverted-source control.
